Ok so it's time to update this API indeed.

Sam, do you want to convert the kwargs arguments here in a full and explicit list?

I think we should have all arguments being provided with either an `encoder_` prefix if the related argument will be fed to the encoder or a `decoder_` prefix if the related arguments will be fed to the decoder.

Bonus point: doing the same explicit conversion for T5 here: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/master/src/transformers/modeling_t5.py#L861-L875

Background: the usage of kwargs came from a copy-past of a logic designed for the generic `modeling_encoder_decoder` which was intended to handle any single stack model and convert it is a encoder-decoder model (still WIP) see here: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/1455#pullrequestreview-307742115. body:
I'm not a fan of allowing `the caller to ignore the seq2seq nature of the model`. In the library, we try to be very explicit on the inner working of the models and I feel like designing the encoder-decoder API is a place where we should be careful to make the right decision so that they are not confused with single-stack models.

I know the Bart model duplicates the input for sequence classification but I think that this is mostly a temporary trick for sequence classification so I don't want this to influence too strongly how we shape the encoder-decoder API in general (for instance, T5 has a different approach). This is related to my comment [here](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/2745#discussion_r378227300) (the other very important part to discuss).

Here is what I would propose:
- let's have a very clean and normal forward loop in the main encoder-decoder `BartModel`, i.e. with explicit `encoder_input_ids` and `decoder_input_ids` and no duplication of `input_ids` inside the forward loop.
- implement the duplication trick of the inputs for both encoder and decoder in the forward loop of `BartForSequenceClassification`.

What do you think?

body:
The way the fairseq code works is that there are two attention masks created in the forward pass for the decoder:
the padding_mask is shaped (bs, seq_len) and causes the model to ignore pad tokens. [1] 
the attention_mask is shaped (src_len, tgt_len) and is used in the decoder to prevent it from attending to future tokens in the target sequence. [2]
#### Plan to consolidate masks:

* force the caller to combine to one attention_mask of shape (bsz, tgt_len, src_len), and achieve API consistency at the cost of a small amount of memory.
* add `def prepare_input_masks_for_masked_lm(input_ids, decoder_input_ids=None, encoder_hidden_states=None)` utility makes masks for callers.

[1] seq_len can be different between encoder and decoder in seq2seq tasks.
[2] A major point of Bart is that the decoder is left-to-right and the encoder is bidirectional. In T5 and UniLM this technique is called prefix LM/the mask is called "causal mask with prefix".

body:
Yes, this is an overwriting of the fit method. The reason is because the custom training loop will not be the same depending if we want distributed on single GPU training. Thus, this overwritten fit will looks like something similar to:
```
if self.distributed:
  loop over distributed_train_step()
else:
  loop over train_step()
```
This is for making the handling of the TF strategies invisible for the user. Thus, making the training distributed or not will be just a boolean in the constructor.
